name: Constitution & Polity
description: Indian Constitution, amendments, and constitutional bodies.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on which date?
questions.explanation: Adopted on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day) and enforced on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

questions.question: Who was the temporary (first) Chairman of the Constituent Assembly when it met in 1946?
questions.explanation: Sachchidananda Sinha presided over the first meeting on 9 December 1946; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was later elected permanent President.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which amendment, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment added Part IVA (Article 51A) with 10 Fundamental Duties; the 86th Amendment added the 11th (education).

questions.question: Article 21 of the Constitution guarantees which right?
options: Right to life and personal liberty
questions.explanation: Article 21 guarantees protection of life and personal liberty; the Supreme Court has expanded it to cover dignity, privacy and a clean environment.

questions.question: Which Article did Dr. B. R. Ambedkar call the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights — the 'heart and soul', per Ambedkar.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV were borrowed from the Constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: The DPSPs were inspired by the Irish Constitution; the Irish example also inspired the nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that 'procedure established by law' must be fair, just and reasonable?
questions.explanation: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) read due process into Article 21, overturning the narrow A. K. Gopalan interpretation.

questions.question: The doctrine that Parliament cannot amend the 'basic structure' of the Constitution was laid down in which case?
questions.explanation: The 13-judge Kesavananda Bharati bench (1973) propounded the basic-structure doctrine, limiting Parliament's amending power under Article 368.

questions.question: The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of whom?
options: Members of the Rajya Sabha only
questions.explanation: The electoral college comprises elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of state legislative assemblies, voting via proportional representation by single transferable vote.

questions.question: The impeachment of the President of India is provided under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 61 provides for impeachment of the President for 'violation of the Constitution' by a special majority of both Houses.

questions.question: Who was the first Attorney General of India (appointed under Article 76)?
questions.explanation: M. C. Setalvad served as the first Attorney General of India from 1950 to 1963 — the longest-serving AG in history.

questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is provided for under which Article, and is often called what?
options: Article 148 — guardian of the public purse
questions.explanation: Article 148 provides for the CAG, who audits the accounts of the Union and the states and is known as the guardian of the public purse.

questions.question: The Governor of a state is appointed by whom?
questions.explanation: Under Article 155, the Governor is appointed by the President and holds office during the President's pleasure.

questions.question: The anti-defection provisions for MPs and MLAs are contained in which Schedule?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Schedule (added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985) provides for disqualification on the ground of defection.

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) constitutionalised which tier of government?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj — gram panchayat, panchayat samiti and zilla parishad.

questions.question: The 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992) relates to which subject?
questions.explanation: The 74th Amendment constitutionalised urban local bodies — municipal corporations, councils and nagar panchayats (Part IXA).

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment (2016) inserted Article 246A and Article 279A, creating the GST regime from 1 July 2017.

questions.question: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment (2019) provides 10% reservation in education and jobs for whom?
questions.explanation: The 103rd Amendment provides up to 10% reservation for EWS among castes/communities not covered by existing reservations.

questions.question: The 106th Constitutional Amendment (2023), the 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam', reserves what share of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and assemblies?
questions.explanation: The 106th Amendment reserves one-third (33%) of seats in the Lok Sabha, state assemblies and the Delhi legislature for women.

questions.question: The 86th Amendment (2002) made free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for which age group?
questions.explanation: It inserted Article 21A (education for children aged 6–14) and added the 11th Fundamental Duty; the RTE Act followed in 2009.
